The same shape affects required-now-parameter-never-defaulted, which reaches care/service.ts (clock-comfort-and-feeding) but not battles/service.ts (fights-and-duels), where energyCostFor lives.

admin-service is 17 rules on src/modules/admin/service.ts, a file 14 of the 34 src-touching commits edit — because adminReset, adminFastForward and adminReverse all live in it. A feature that only needs 'adminReset must cover your new table' pays for the whole operator-refund model. Splitting ledger.ts and index.ts out into their own doc was the only file-level cut available and it does not touch this.

The harness rules do not fire on the ~115 test files that use the harness. tests/** as a glob appears nowhere on purpose. The justification is that the fakes THROW on a lifecycle violation, so harness-lifecycle-enforced and harness-option-getters-from-builder are self-enforcing; that argument does not cover test-live-rest-only-gallery or router-hooks-skip-direct-execute, which a test author genuinely can miss silently.

no-test-fixtures-in-assets sits in art-asset-files, but the mistake — a writeFileSync/rmSync onto a committed asset path, which vitest's parallel forks let another file observe — is made in a test file that fires its own subject's doc. Only tests/images.test.ts and tests/asset-variants.test.ts, which nobody stages a fixture from, will surface it.

ctx-sleep-injected and sender-fakes-hand-rolled-grep are in notify-and-runtime, keyed on notify.ts/context.ts/index.ts. The other Ctx construction sites (tests/harness.ts, scripts/test-live.ts) and four of the five hand-rolled Sender fakes live in files that fire other docs, so a Ctx or Sender shape change approached from the test side surfaces neither.

filtered-lists-need-their-own-page-row is in embed-payload-builders. Both existing instances are covered (dex/embeds.ts and admin/ledger.ts are both in that glob), but the 'do not widen pageRow' half only fires when src/core/paginate.ts itself is edited, and a third filtered pager built inside an index.ts would see nothing — which is exactly how the dex pager shipped broken the first time.

THE PARTITION IS PART ENUMERATION, SO IT DOES NOT FULLY SELF-EXTEND. Directory globs and six filename families (tests/alert-*, tests/battle-*, tests/daily-*, tests/render-*, tests/season*, tests/autocomplete-*) pick up new files on their own; every other test file is named individually. A new tests/foo.test.ts, a new src/core/*.ts or a new src/data/*.ts orphans silently until someone adds it to a glob list, and a badly-named future test lands in the wrong doc with no warning. That manual upkeep is the price of killing the tests/** wallpaper.

docs/gameplay.md pays 39 lines across 19 touches — the third-heaviest item in the repo by touches x cost — to surface three of the four rules that name it. The fourth, sweep-never-settles-escapes, is in timers-and-alerts and is not surfaced there, so the doc can still be edited into disagreement with the escapes behaviour it documents.

species-and-dex is thin: 5 rules for 63 files. A species-only commit that ships no art will not surface dino-art-archetype-diet-with-species-override (art-resolver), the rule that explains why a new species costs no new art — the pair is only complete when the WebP lands in the same change. Likewise escrow-and-item-moves is an honest grab-bag of six modules named for what they do rather than what they are, exactly as the by-file ruling permits; a reader expecting a tidy table of contents will not find one there.

The per-commit figures (median 185 for src-touching commits) are measured on squash merges of entire features, because this repo's main branch has no small-commit history to score against. The per-file numbers (median 23) are the ones a PreToolUse hook actually injects, since it matches one file per tool call; treat the commit numbers as a worst case that is never paid in one shot.
